key: And he answered: ‘Thou shalt not smite them; hast thou taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow those whom thou wouldest smite? set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, and go to their master.’
s: When the king of Israel asks whether to kill the Aramean troops Elisha has led blinded into Samaria, the prophet answers; Metzudat David, on 6:22, reads it as denying the king any claim on men he never captured, whom a miracle had brought.

evidence.words: האשר שבית. האם הם אשר שבית אתה, לשתכה בהם, הלא בנס הובאו, ומה לך להם
evidence.gloss: “Hast thou taken captive”: are these men the ones thou hast taken captive, that thou shouldest smite them? Were they not brought here by a miracle, and what hast thou to do with them?

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 2 Kings 6:22, at [314,22]). Metzudat David on 6:22 asks whether these are men the king captured, says they were brought by a miracle, and asks what the king has to do with them: the reading (no claim on men he never captured, whom a miracle had brought) is his, without drift. Radak on the same verse gives the same question of right (מה דין יש לך בהם) without the miracle; Rashi asks whether it is the king’s custom to kill captives; neither contradicts. Plain sense matches 6:18 to 6:21 (blinded, led to Samaria, king asks whether to smite); the killing question is stated plainly. 43 words; entry-check ok.
